The first breath, and the last amen.

sheet: How long have we sought the Eternal Father,
who created us to seek Him?
How long through silence, shadow, and the dark?
We have carried His name —
but have we known His heart?
In one voice, in one mind —
we come home to Him.
God is not a fable told against the silence —
He was moved by love to give us life.
He weeps when His children go astray.
More present than doubt, more enduring than distance —
the God who feels is the God who remains faithful.
He sent us His Son — no shadow, no pretense —
Christ wore our flesh and was sore amazed,
as He knelt in the garden’s dark to know us.
His living mission: to gather us with Him.
This we hold with one voice and one mind:
He is real. He is near. He has not left us behind.
Through the shadows and doubt, in the light and the clear —
one faith, one hope — we hold each other here.
His grace is not a transaction — it is His power.
It enters the cracks and rebuilds us from within.
We are not left where His grace first found us —
we are formed by the grace we were made for.
He calls us to ripeness, to wholeness, to flourishing —
His image growing in us day by day.
Not crushed by impossible standards,
but gently becoming beneath His steady gaze.
He said life eternal begins now, not later —
to know the living God is where it starts.
We do not have to wait for what He promised —
the Kingdom is at hand for willing hearts.
The vessels who bore His word were cracked —
earthen jars, just as we are.
Yet the water runs pure though the vessel is clay,
and the wellspring has never run dry.
He sets His table for all of His children;
He denies none who come — not a single one.
All are alike unto God in this gathering —
the lost and the seeking, the weak and the strong.
He builds up the Church of the Lamb,
gathering us from every nation and shore.
No gatekeepers stand at the door He has opened —
all who are His He has called, and will shelter.
By this the world will know we belong to Him —
not by doctrine, traditions, or names,
but by love that carries the weight of another,
that mourns with the mourning and shoulders the shame.

this broken soul was never mine to mend.
So Jesus, keep me turning to You,
walking the path that leads me home.
Grace was never wages waiting
at the ending of the fight;
grace is strength inside the struggle,
grace is power for the climb.
Line upon line You remake me —
You are not done with me yet —
not a Judge who counts my failures,
but a Father who forgives.
And the sins I laid before You,
You remember them no more,
till I stand within Your glory,
unashamed before the Lord.
So keep me turning, Lord, morning and night —
till my whole heart belongs to You.

arrangements.label: Cinematic Orchestral — Piano-Led with Full Orchestra Build
sheet: I don't have pretty words or practiced speech,
No memorized petition, polished bright.
Just everything that's tangled in my heart—
The gratitude, the worry, and the fight.
He told me God don't care about the language,
The Lord looks past the stumblings of the soul.
So I speak the way a child speaks to a Father—
Honest, reaching, longing to be whole.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The first breath, and the last amen.
On bended knees or striving through the dark,
Just talk to Him — and then
Be still, and learn to listen,
For the Spirit speaks within.
The Father hears you, every word—
So pour your whole heart out.
Sometimes I bow my head before the sunrise.
Sometimes I cry for help with no time to kneel.
Sometimes it's just a whisper while I'm working—
A constant prayer for everything I feel.
He said to pray in closets, not for show,
To come with real intent and not with pride.
So here behind the door, I bring my burdens,
And lay them down with nothing left to hide.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The first breath, and the last amen.
On bended knees or striving through the dark,
Just talk to Him — and then
Be still, and learn to listen,
For the Spirit speaks within.
The Father hears you, every word—
So pour your whole heart out.
I used to think that prayer was only asking,
Sending words like postcards, never received.
But then I paused — and something stirred inside me,
A still, small voice I'd never learned to heed.
He speaks to mind and heart at once,
A burning and a peace.
The Spirit carries back His word
Until the questions cease.
This is how the Father answers—
Not in thunder, but in light.
He said, "Ask, and I will show you."
And He meant it. And He's right.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The offering that never ends.
He knew my needs before I spoke—
And still He calls me friend.
So speak, and then be still and listen,
For the heavens aren't sealed tight.
The God who spoke to prophets old
Still speaks from the light.
Pray always… listen well.
Think things over, and then ask God.
He'll cause your heart to burn
if it's right and true.
He's the same God He's always been.
And He is waiting for you now…
when you're ready.
In the name of Jesus Christ,
Amen.

arrangements.title: The Soul's Sincere Desire
arrangements.label: Americana Folk — Fingerpicked Guitar and Front Porch Testimony
sheet: I don't have pretty words or practiced speech,
No memorized petition, polished bright.
Just everything that's tangled in my heart—
The gratitude, the worry, and the fight.
He told me God don't care about the language,
The Lord looks past the stumblings of the soul.
So I speak the way a child speaks to a Father—
Honest, reaching, longing to be whole.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The first breath, and the last amen.
On bended knees or striving through the dark,
Just talk to Him — and then
Be still, and learn to listen,
For the Spirit speaks within.
The Father hears you, every word—
So pour your whole heart out.
Sometimes I bow my head before the sunrise.
Sometimes I cry for help with no time to kneel.
Sometimes it's just a whisper while I'm working—
A constant prayer for everything I feel.
He said to pray in closets, not for show,
To come with real intent and not with pride.
So here behind the door, I bring my burdens,
And lay them down with nothing left to hide.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The first breath, and the last amen.
On bended knees or striving through the dark,
Just talk to Him — and then
Be still, and learn to listen,
For the Spirit speaks within.
The Father hears you, every word—
So pour your whole heart out.
I used to think that prayer was only asking,
Sending words like postcards, never received.
But then I paused — and something stirred inside me,
A still, small voice I'd never learned to heed.
He speaks to mind and heart at once,
A burning and a peace.
The Spirit carries back His word
Until the questions cease.
This is how the Father answers—
Not in thunder, but in light.
He said, "Ask, and I will show you."
And He meant it. And He's right.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The offering that never ends.
He knew my needs before I spoke—
And still He calls me friend.
So speak, and then be still and listen,
For the heavens aren't sealed tight.
The God who spoke to prophets old
Still speaks from the light.
Pray always… listen well.
Think things over, and then ask God.
He'll cause your heart to burn
if it's right and true.
He's the same God He's always been.
And He is waiting for you now…
when you're ready.
In the name of Jesus Christ,
Amen.

arrangements.title: One Voice, One Mind
arrangements.label: Interfaith Anthem
sheet: How long have we sought the Eternal Father,
who created us to seek Him?
How long through silence, shadow, and the dark?
We have carried His name —
but have we known His heart?
In one voice, in one mind —
we come home to Him.
God is not a fable told against the silence —
He was moved by love to give us life.
He weeps when His children go astray.
More present than doubt, more enduring than distance —
the God who feels is the God who remains faithful.
He sent us His Son — no shadow, no pretense —
Christ wore our flesh and was sore amazed,
as He knelt in the garden’s dark to know us.
His living mission: to gather us with Him.
This we hold with one voice and one mind:
He is real. He is near. He has not left us behind.
Through the shadows and doubt, in the light and the clear —
one faith, one hope — we hold each other here.
His grace is not a transaction — it is His power.
It enters the cracks and rebuilds us from within.
We are not left where His grace first found us —
we are formed by the grace we were made for.
He calls us to ripeness, to wholeness, to flourishing —
His image growing in us day by day.
Not crushed by impossible standards,
but gently becoming beneath His steady gaze.
He said life eternal begins now, not later —
to know the living God is where it starts.
We do not have to wait for what He promised —
the Kingdom is at hand for willing hearts.
The vessels who bore His word were cracked —
earthen jars, just as we are.
Yet the water runs pure though the vessel is clay,
and the wellspring has never run dry.
He sets His table for all of His children;
He denies none who come — not a single one.
All are alike unto God in this gathering —
the lost and the seeking, the weak and the strong.
He builds up the Church of the Lamb,
gathering us from every nation and shore.
No gatekeepers stand at the door He has opened —
all who are His He has called, and will shelter.
By this the world will know we belong to Him —
not by doctrine, traditions, or names,
but by love that carries the weight of another,
that mourns with the mourning and shoulders the shame.
And that —
they all —
may be —
ONE —
As the Father and Son.
Not one in opinion — but one in His love,
that never abandons and burns bright always.
We see through a glass, and we see only in part.
Our knowing is dim, but our knowing is real.
Our holding is honest. We hold as we are able,
and we walk by His light that lives in our heart.
And when there is nothing but stubborn hope left —
when faith is a wrestle, but our grip will not weaken —
we cling to His covenant — anyway — always —
for He gathers His own, even when our strength gives way.
This we hold with one voice and one mind:
He is real. He is near. He has not left us behind.
Through the shadows and doubt, in the light and the clear —
one faith, one hope — we hold each other here.
That they may all be one — as the Father and Son —
this is the prayer that gathers us in one.
We hold on. He holds more. We press on. He goes before.
In one voice — He is real.
In one mind — He is near.
He has not left us behind.
In one voice, in one mind — we come home to Him.

arrangements.title: Two Halves of a Whole
arrangements.label: Americana Folk
arrangements.source: Ch 3 - Two Halves of a Whole
sheet: I've walked the avenues of life,
I've tasted rain and summer's heat.
I've gathered pearls of wisdom, simply beautiful,
And laid them down here at the Teacher's feet.
The world is organized in such complexity,
The Architect is found in every stone.
But even when survival needs are met,
A hunger stays for something still unknown.
For truth is knowledge as things really are,
A light that shines on what is yet to come.
Science isn't blind and faith isn't lame
When we see them both as one.
It's a fuller way of walking on the road
Where every path to truth is joined together.
We're chasing down the meaning of our days,
By the love of God directed, now and ever.
I've built my intellectual altars to the mind
Through philosophy and arts and the sciences.
I've analyzed the patterns and the laws
And let my thinking be my sole reliance.
But academic means can only go so far,
They're limited by things we can't perceive.
We're ever learning, never coming to the truth
Without the courage to truly believe.
Now I'm standing at the ceiling of the framework,
Looking through the window at the rain.
Reason is a shadow in the moonlight
If it cannot take away the pain.
Why is there something rather than nothing at all?
Does who I am persist beyond the grave?
I'm reaching for the eyes that have been hidden,
For the spirit that the Savior came to save.
I choose to experiment upon the word.
I choose the foresight of the prophecy.
The spirit speaks what senses never heard—
It's the power of God that sets the seeker free!
So I'll walk in wondering humility,
Recognizing that I know so very little.
The world may shift like shadows on the wall,
But a simple truth is resting in the middle.
Great ignorance might lead a man to fear,
And knowledge brings a measure of our sorrow.
But wisdom brings a peace that's resting here
And a hope for every bright tomorrow.
Life has grand purpose.
A beautiful and simple way.
In the name of Jesus Christ,
Amen.

"Be ye therefore perfect" kept me striving, kept me small,
Till I learned the word means finished—not "you'd better never fall."
Blessed means flourishing—that's the word He chose.
Not "make yourself worthy," not "put on better clothes."
It's the life that's genuinely good, the life He came to give—
Not a standard you can't reach, but a way to truly live.
This is what you were made to be—
Not flawless, but completed—not fallen, but free.
The kingdom is yours. The kingdom is now.
He's finishing what He started—let me show you how.
It starts with honest seeing—poor in spirit means you're real.
You stop the performance, drop the mask, and say the things you feel.
The Lord is near the brokenhearted—that's the door that lets Him in.
And comfort isn't fixing you—it's God beside you as you grow.
You can loosen up your grip—meekness isn't being weak.
Strength governed by discipline, power restrained by wisdom.
And the hunger runs in you like a river going dry—
The soul that thirsts for righteousness will never be denied.
This is what you were made to be—
Not flawless, but completed—not fallen, but free.
The kingdom is yours. The kingdom is now.
He's finishing what He started—let me show you how.
Mercy costs you something—it always does, it always will.
It owns debts it didn't earn, love that satisfies justice.
But the pure in heart—they'll see Him.
They'll see Him.
Beholding changes everything—from glory into glory.
His image in your countenance, created in His image.
Now He sends you out as peacemaker—the highest name He gives.
Not avoiding all the conflict, but in the middle of it—this is how He lives.
The road will cost you something—the faithful always pay—
But "theirs is the kingdom of heaven"—the same words from His sermon.
The heart that was broken is the heart that now endures.
The grip you finally loosened—now the open hands are yours.
This is what you were made to be—
Not flawless, but completed—not fallen, but free.
The kingdom is yours. The kingdom is now.
He finished what He started. He showed us how.
You were made for this.
Not perfection—completion. Not flawless—flourishing.
The journey is the becoming. And He promised to finish it.
In the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.

arrangements.label: Contemporary Christian
sheet: The greatest Teacher who ever lived
stood on a mountain and gave His class
the hardest assignment they'd ever receive —
how to become like God.
We understand the assignment.
I read the Sermon on the Mount
And felt the weight of every word
Love your enemy, turn your cheek,
Be perfect — that's what I heard
I tried to clench my heart up tight
And fix the anger on my own
But willpower broke where grace begins —
I couldn't change my heart alone
Peter asked, "What kind of person will you be?"
Let your life speak louder than your words
Be the salt — be the light — don't hide what He gave you
I'm gonna build my life upon His rock
He didn't come to toss the law —
He came to take it to the heart
Not just the act but the desire,
Not just the deed but every part
The Higher Law is way too high
For any soul to reach alone —
It's what God's grace looks like inside
A heart that's let the Savior in
Peter asked, "What kind of person will you be?"
Bring the heart you cannot fix yourself
Let Him write His law where willpower never could
I'm gonna build my life upon His rock
He doesn't stand with folded arms
And watch you struggle up the slope
He walks beside you — He's walked this road —
Every step, He is your hope
Ask and you'll receive
Seek and you will find
Knock and it'll open —
He's been waiting all this time
Peter asked, "What kind of person will you be?"
Pray where no one sees, give where no one knows
The Father who sees in secret — He sees you right now
I'm gonna build my life upon His rock
I knew the right things all those years
And did so few of them
The storm came through and showed the cracks
In what I'd built on sand
Rebuilding's slow — it's daily work —
One small obedient choice
Not waiting for the spectacular —
Just following His voice
Peter asked, "What kind of person will you be?"
Do the thing you know, not just what you've heard
Every faithful step lays another stone
I'm gonna build my life upon His rock

It's a standard you can grow into.

walks beside you as you learn to live it.

sheet: I've walked the avenues of life,
I've tasted rain and summer's heat.
I've gathered pearls of wisdom, simply beautiful,
And laid them down here at the Teacher's feet.
The world is organized in such complexity,
The Architect is found in every stone.
But even when survival needs are met,
A hunger stays for something still unknown.
For truth is knowledge as things really are,
A light that shines on what is yet to come.

We're ever learning, never coming to the truth

Now I'm standing at the ceiling of the framework,
Looking through the window at the rain.
Reason is a shadow in the moonlight
If it cannot take away the pain.
Why is there something rather than nothing at all?
Does who I am persist beyond the grave?
I'm reaching for the eyes that have been hidden,
For the spirit that the Savior came to save.
I choose to experiment upon the word.
I choose the foresight of the prophecy.
The spirit speaks what senses never heard—
It's the power of God that sets the seeker free!

But a simple truth is resting in the middle.

And knowledge brings a measure of our sorrow.
But wisdom brings a peace that's resting here
And a hope for every bright tomorrow.
Life has grand purpose.
A beautiful and simple way.
In the name of Jesus Christ,
Amen.

arrangements.title: Keep Me Turning to You
arrangements.label: Piano Ballad
arrangements.source: Ch 15 - Keep Me Turning to You
sheet: I used to wait for the breaking point,
the edge of shame and desperation,
before I could lift my voice to You,
falling into Your healing arms.
But Your mercy outlasts dark nights —
it knocks at my door each morning.
Now I know, turning to You isn't weakness;
it isn't crawling back in shame.
I stand tallest on my knees in prayer.
Worldly sorrow heals no wounds,
it's just a cell that locks me in;
it never once has made me clean —
it only names my grief and sins.
But the sorrow that comes from Heaven
is a door thrown open wide;
it does not leave me in despair —
and Heaven whispers gently: come unto me.
So keep me turning, Lord, morning and night —
till my whole heart leans to You.
When I wander, when I'm weary, when I'm cold,
Savior, help me turn to what is warm and true.
I never could climb alone to Heaven;
this broken soul was never mine to mend.
So Jesus, keep me turning to You,
walking the path that leads me home.

there are words I will not say,
and the weight of what I'm hiding
only grows from day to day.
So I put these things upon Your altar,
and I name them in the light —
and the things I thought would ruin me
loosed their hold on me this night.
So keep me turning, Lord, morning and night —
till my whole heart leans to You.
When I wander, when I'm weary, when I'm cold,
Savior, help me turn to what is warm and true.
I never could climb alone to Heaven;
this broken soul was never mine to mend.
So Jesus, keep me turning to You,
walking the path that leads me home.

grace is strength inside the struggle,
grace is power for the climb.
Line upon line You remake me —
You are not done with me yet —
not a Judge who counts my failures,
but a Father who forgives.
And the sins I laid before You,
You remember them no more,
till I stand within Your glory,
unashamed before the Lord.
So keep me turning, Lord, morning and night —
till my whole heart belongs to You.

not because I never wandered,
but because Your mercy stayed;
Jesus, You kept me turning,
till I stand before You saved.
New every morning, Your mercies never end.
New every morning — turn me home again.

sheet: They watched Him rise until the cloud received Him.
And stood there staring at an empty sky.
Two angels came and asked them gently.
Why are you looking up?
What looked like leaving was a promise kept:
I will not leave you here alone.
Two walked a road with hearts too heavy to see.

He ever lives — He is not gone.

arrangements.title: Keep Me Turning to You
arrangements.label: Folk Hymn Duet
arrangements.source: Ch 15 - Keep Me Turning to You (alt)
sheet: I used to wait for the breaking point,
the edge of shame and desperation,
before I could lift my voice to You,
falling into Your healing arms.
But Your mercy outlasts dark nights —
it knocks at my door each morning.
Now I know, turning to You isn't weakness;
it isn't crawling back in shame.
I stand tallest on my knees in prayer.
Worldly sorrow heals no wounds,
it's just a cell that locks me in;
it never once has made me clean —
it only names my grief and sins.
But the sorrow that comes from Heaven
is a door thrown open wide;
it does not leave me in despair —
and Heaven whispers gently: come unto me.
So keep me turning, Lord, morning and night —
till my whole heart leans to You.
When I wander, when I'm weary, when I'm cold,
Savior, help me turn to what is warm and true.
I never could climb alone to Heaven;
this broken soul was never mine to mend.
So Jesus, keep me turning to You,
walking the path that leads me home.
There are choices I keep in shadow,
there are words I will not say,
and the weight of what I'm hiding
only grows from day to day.
So I put these things upon Your altar,
and I name them in the light —
and the things I thought would ruin me
loosed their hold on me this night.
So keep me turning, Lord, morning and night —
till my whole heart leans to You.
When I wander, when I'm weary, when I'm cold,
Savior, help me turn to what is warm and true.
I never could climb alone to Heaven;
this broken soul was never mine to mend.
So Jesus, keep me turning to You,
walking the path that leads me home.
Grace was never wages waiting
at the ending of the fight;
grace is strength inside the struggle,
grace is power for the climb.
Line upon line You remake me —
You are not done with me yet —
not a Judge who counts my failures,
but a Father who forgives.
And the sins I laid before You,
You remember them no more,
till I stand within Your glory,
unashamed before the Lord.
So keep me turning, Lord, morning and night —
till my whole heart belongs to You.
And when I stand within Your glory,
let me fear Your face no more —
not because I never wandered,
but because Your mercy stayed;
Jesus, You kept me turning,
till I stand before You saved.
New every morning, Your mercies never end.
New every morning — turn me home again.
In the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
